prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single “best” site — pick the platform that matches your priorities.
  - Want whole homes for families or groups? Vrbo tends to focus on full properties.
  - Want a mix of apartments, unique stays and local hosts? Airbnb is strongest.
  - Want hotel-like inventory, last-minute availability and lots of pay-at-property options? Booking.com is best.
- Regardless of platform, use the same checklist to find a reliable host/listing.

Which platform is best for different priorities
- Families / whole-home rentals / beach houses: Vrbo
  - Pros: mostly whole homes, family-oriented filters, clear occupancy rules.
  - Cons: fewer shared/unique experiences, host vetting varies by market.
- Unique/host-driven stays, local experiences, community features: Airbnb
  - Pros: strong host ecosystem (Superhosts), experiences, good search filters.
  - Cons: service fees can be high; some recent policy/price changes.
- Hotels + apartments + instant bookings + flexible payments: Booking.com
  - Pros: lots of inventory, pay-at-property options, strong last-minute deals, real guest review volume.
  - Cons: many different property types; listings range from hotels to private homes (check carefully).

How to find a good host — a practical checklist (do this before you book)
1. Read reviews (not just the score)
   - Read recent reviews and several older ones. Look for repeated themes (cleanliness, accuracy of description, responsiveness).
   - Beware: 1–3 reviews only = risk. A long string of five-star one-line reviews can be suspicious.
2. Check host credibility
   - Look for Superhost / Top Host / Premier Partner badges and high response rate.
   - Verified ID on Airbnb, host profile completeness, number of listings and how long they’ve been hosting.
3. Confirm listing accuracy
   - Check the photos carefully (windows, layout, views). If photos are sparse or stock-looking, ask for more.
   - Use map view and Street View (Google Maps) to verify neighborhood and building exterior.
4. Read the fine print
   - Total price = nightly rate + cleaning fee + service fees + local taxes. Compare totals across platforms.
   - Check cancellation policy and refund conditions (strict vs flexible).
   - Check house rules, check-in/check-out times, extra guest/pet rules.
5. Test responsiveness before booking
   - Message the host with a specific question (arrival time, parking, elevator access). Quick, clear responses are a strong signal.
6. Look for red flags
   - Host asks to pay outside the platform, pushes to switch to messaging off-platform, mismatched photos/text, huge last-minute discounts that seem too good to be true.
   - Reviews mentioning “host never met us / access issues” or safety problems.
7. Verify safety features
   - Confirm locks, smoke/CO detectors, outdoor lighting, and any security cameras (hosts must disclose cameras).
8. For longer stays or higher-value bookings
   - Ask for a simple written agreement confirming dates, rate, deposit, cancellation terms.
   - Consider refundable damage protection offered through the platform or third-party travel insurance.
9. Document condition on arrival
   - Take photos/videos of any damage on day one and message the host and platform immediately if there’s an issue.

Platform-specific protection & payment tips
- Always pay through the platform. Never transfer money or accept wiring/PayPal/Venmo requests.
- Airbnb: has Host Guarantee and Resolution Center but read limits; cancellation and refund policies vary by listing.
- Vrbo: offers damage protection options; policies depend on the host.
- Booking.com: often has flexible payment options and hotel-like booking protections; private-home policies can vary widely.
- For disputes, contact the platform first and keep photos/communications.

Price & timing tips
- Compare total price across platforms (cleaning fees can break a good nightly rate).
- Book early for peak travel; for off-season or last-minute, you can often find deals.
- Use flexible dates and set price alerts if your trip is flexible.
- For stays longer than ~28–30 nights, hosts often offer big discounts — negotiate politely.

If you’d like, I can:
- Recommend which platform is best for your specific trip if you tell me destination, dates, group size, and priorities (budget, whole place vs room, pets, etc.).
- Review 2–3 listing links and point out any concerns in the listing, reviews or price breakdown.
